1.q: שִׁמְעָ֤⁠ה יְהוָ֨ה ׀ צֶ֗דֶק הַקְשִׁ֥יבָ⁠ה רִנָּתִ֗⁠י הַאֲזִ֥ינָ⁠ה תְפִלָּתִ֑⁠י
1.note: These are imperatives, but they communicate polite requests rather than commands. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates polite requests. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please listen, Yahweh, to righteousness. Please pay attention to my cry! Please give ear to my prayer]
See how you translated this word in 11:7.

David is using **Give ear** as a common expression of his culture to mean “listen” or “pay attention.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Listen to my prayer] or [Hear my prayer]

Here, **lips** represents the person who is speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Give ear to my prayer, since I speak without deceit] or [Give ear to my prayer, for I am not deceiving you]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **deceit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [lips that do not deceive] or [lips that speak truthfully]

2.q: מִ֭⁠לְּ⁠פָנֶי⁠ךָ מִשְׁפָּטִ֣⁠י יֵצֵ֑א עֵ֝ינֶ֗י⁠ךָ תֶּחֱזֶ֥ינָה מֵישָׁרִֽים
2.note: By using **let**, David is expressing what he desires or prays will happen. See the discussion in the introduction to this book about “let” and “may” and follow the decision of your team of how a speaker will express in this context what he wants someone to do. Alternate translation: [My vindication should come from your face; your eyes should see rightly]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **vindication**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a declaration of my innocence]

Here, **your face** represents God’s presence or his judgment. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from your presence] or [from you]

Here, **eyes** represents God’s ability to judge or evaluate. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [may you judge rightly]

3.note: Here, **my heart** represents David’s thoughts, feelings, and motives. You may have a comparable expression in your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my thoughts] or [my inner being]

By **you have visited me in the night**, David means that God examines his heart and thoughts during the quiet hours when his true character is most evident. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [you have examined my heart at night]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context (as in the ULT) if that would be clearer in your language.

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [you have tested me and have detected nothing that displeases you]

Here, **mouth** represents “speech.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I have purposed that I will not transgress with my speech]

4.note: The psalmist is not referring to a specific **man**. He means people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [mankind]

4.q: בִּ⁠דְבַ֣ר שְׂפָתֶ֑י⁠ךָ אֲנִ֥י שָׁ֝מַ֗רְתִּי אָרְח֥וֹת פָּרִֽיץ
4.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [I have kept myself away from the paths of the violent by the word of your lips]

Here, **word** represents God’s oral or written communication. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by your word] or [by what you have spoken]

Here David is speaking of how people live as if they were actually **paths** that they walk on. The phrase **paths of the violent** refers to living in a way that is characterized by unjust violence against innocent people. (David performed violent actions in the context of war but this refers to non-military violence.) If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a violent way of life] or [a destructive lifestyle characterized by violence]

David is using the adjective **violent** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [violent people]

5.note: Here David is speaking as if his obedience to God were actually **steps** that **hold firmly to** God’s **tracks**. (God’s **tracks** refer to the actions and lifestyle that God desires for people.) Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have consistently obeyed your commands; I have not disobeyed you]

6.note: The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because you will answer me God, I have called upon you]

This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please incline]
Here, **ear** represents hearing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Listen to me]
By **my speech**, David means his prayer. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [listen to my prayer]

7.note: The implication of **Set apart** is that David wants God to show his covenant faithfulness in a special or extraordinary way to help him in his current situation. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Show your covenant faithfulness in a special way] or [Display your covenant faithfulness remarkably]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **covenant faithfulness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [all the ways you are faithful to your covenant]
Here, **hand** represents the power of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [by your power]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones seeking refuge in you from those rising up against them]

Here David is speaking of **the ones seeking refuge** in God as if they were literally seeking physical shelter or protection. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [those who trust in you for protection]

David is using **those rising up** as a common expression of his culture to mean “those who oppose” or “enemies.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from those taking action against them] or [from those trying to harm them]

8.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the pupil of your eye** is carefully protected, so David wants God to protect him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [Protect me carefully] or [Guard me protectively]

David is speaking as if Yahweh were a bird and he were one of its chicks. Your language may have a comparable expression you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [protect me as a mother bird protects its chicks by covering them with its wings]

9.note: Here the phrase **from the faces of** was a common expression meaning “from the presence of” or “because of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression that does have that meaning or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the presence of]

David is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean wicked people. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [wicked people] or [wicked men]

David is using the term **my soul** to mean his entire person from the perspective of his spiritual and emotional existence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to me]

10.note: Here, **fat** represents their hearts or inner beings that have become hardened and unfeeling. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They have hardened their hearts] or [Their hearts have become unfeeling]

It might seem that the expression **with their mouths they speak** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [they speak with pride]

11.note: By **our steps**, David means the steps that both he and his enemies are taking as they move. The enemies are surrounding him at every point along their path. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [They have surrounded me now wherever we go] or [They have surrounded me at every point along our path]

Some ancient manuscripts read **They have surrounded me**. The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts read “They have surrounded us.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

By **Their eyes they have set, crouching down to the earth**, the psalmist means that his enemies are watching him carefully and getting ready to attack him like wild animals that crouch low before they pounce on their prey. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [They stare at me intently, crouched low and ready to attack]

12.q: דִּמְיֹנ֗⁠וֹ כְּ֭⁠אַרְיֵה יִכְס֣וֹף לִ⁠טְר֑וֹף וְ֝⁠כִ⁠כְפִ֗יר יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּ⁠מִסְתָּרִֽים
12.note: The pronoun **His** refers to the wicked person described in the previous verses. The pronoun **he** refers to this same wicked person. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [The wicked person’s likeness is as a lion, the wicked person longs to tear; and as a young lion the wicked person is dwelling in hiding places]

12.q: דִּמְיֹנ֗⁠וֹ כְּ֭⁠אַרְיֵה יִכְס֣וֹף לִ⁠טְר֑וֹף וְ֝⁠כִ⁠כְפִ֗יר יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּ⁠מִסְתָּרִֽים
12.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a lion** longs to tear apart its prey, so the wicked person’s **likeness** resembles a lion that longs to attack. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [He is like a lion that longs to tear apart its prey, and like a young lion hiding and waiting to attack]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [he longs to tear his prey]

13.q: קוּמָ֤⁠ה יְהוָ֗ה קַדְּמָ֣⁠ה פָ֭נָי⁠ו הַכְרִיעֵ֑⁠הוּ פַּלְּטָ֥⁠ה נַ֝פְשִׁ֗⁠י
13.note: Here David is using imperative forms **Arise**, **confront**, **make him bow down**, and **Rescue** to communicate polite requests to God rather than commands. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please arise, Yahweh, please confront his face, please make him bow down! Please rescue my soul]

Here, **his face** represents his presence or confronting him directly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [confront him directly] or [face him in battle]

By **make him bow down** David means “throw him to the ground” or “cause him to fall to the ground” and probably means “fall to the ground dead.” You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [make him fall down dead] or [cause him to fall to the ground defeated]

David is using one part of a person, his **soul**, to mean all of him in the act of being rescued. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me]

David is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [from wicked people] or [from wicked men]

Here, **sword** represents power or strength used for powerful, violent action. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [with your power]

14.q: מִֽ⁠מְתִ֥ים יָדְ⁠ךָ֨ ׀ יְהוָ֡ה מִֽ⁠מְתִ֬ים מֵ⁠חֶ֗לֶד חֶלְקָ֥⁠ם בַּֽ⁠חַיִּים֮
14.note: David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Rescue me from men by your hand, Yahweh, from men of this world whose portion is in this life]

Here, **hand** represents the power of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Rescue me from evil men by your power Yahweh] or [From men, with your power Yahweh]

Here the psalmist is speaking of God providing abundantly for his people as if he would literally with his treasure **fill their belly**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you abundantly provide for them from your riches]

Here the masculine term **sons** has a generic sense that includes both sons and daughters. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both sons and daughters. Alternate translation: [with children]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **abundance**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [their abundant possessions] or [great wealth]

15.note: David is using the adjective **righteousness** as a noun to mean a state or condition of being righteous. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase as in the UST.
David is using **your face** to represent all of God. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will see you]
Some Bible scholars think that the phrase **when I awake** is a reference to David’s future bodily resurrection. If it would help your readers, you could include a footnote explaining this.

The implication is that David will be satisfied when he sees God. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I will be satisfied with your presence]
